clue.text: Promise leads to halting puzzle

parts.note: to give your word is to make a promise
game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg, so halting in walk

explanation.surface: A broken pledge brings a negotiation to a standstill and leaves everyone baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME here is the old adjective meaning lame or crippled, as in 'a game leg', not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A word game such as an anagram or acrostic is a kind of puzzle played with letters.

clue.text: Vaguely pious restraining of French religious group

indicators.note: restraining means holding something in, so one piece sits within the other
done vaguely, the letters of pious lose their fixed order and are rearranged

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A hint that some devout body is only loosely holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Catholic institution, a religious organisation founded in Spain in 1928.

clue.text: Charitable people overlooking new openings

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring or leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: donors are people who give to charity

explanation.surface: Philanthropists with a view over some new shop or venue launches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' looks like a view from above, but it means ignoring: DONORS ignores N.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are entrances, the gaps in walls through which people pass.

clue.text: Sporting venue, live, hosting international before end of game

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the next one in the answer
hosting means having a guest inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: are is a form of to be, to exist or live

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of game

explanation.surface: A sports ground broadcasting live with an international match shortly before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the racecourse near Liverpool that holds the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous horse-racing course, a place where sport is held.

clue.text: Consume Evian water around end of night, then pee

indicators.note: around says the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: Evian is French, and the French for water is eau

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of night

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is spelt out

explanation.surface: Drink bottled mineral water late at night and then need the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evian' marks the water as French, giving EAU; 'pee' is the letter P spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is to finish food entirely, to consume all of it.

clue.text: Japanese language requires year on island

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: Visiting an island means learning Japanese within a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is the largest of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy.

clue.text: Articles variously blocking examiners for about four weeks

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, so the articles sit inside the examiners word
variously says the articles go in at different points rather than together

parts.note: a jury examines the evidence in a trial
an and a are the indefinite articles
a is the other indefinite article, put in at a second point

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces scattered among a panel of assessors for a month or so.
explanation.walkthrough: Variously means the two articles are not inserted together but at separate points in the examiners word, one after its first letter and one after its second.
explanation.definitionFit: January is a month of thirty-one days, roughly four and a half weeks.

clue.text: Table decoration put over drink for the unsuccessful?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over places the first piece on top of the next

parts.note: a runner is a long strip of cloth laid along a table
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Laying a tablecloth across a glass for the losers.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners-up came second, so they did not win: the question mark admits they still did well.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who finish behind the winner of a race or contest fail to take first place.

clue.text: Each guided round by husband? Showed sign of relief, perhaps

indicators.note: round says the first pieces go around the next

parts.note: by as in multiplied by, three by four, gives the times sign X
to guide is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: Each person was steered around by a spouse and then sighed with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' gives X as in multiplication, 'three by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out a long sigh is how people commonly show their relief.

clue.text: Catch linked to name on aperitif

indicators.note: linked to joins the pieces, here with the net piece at the end

parts.note: to dub is to give a name to
to catch fish you net them

explanation.surface: Catching something linked to a name printed on a drinks label.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubonnet is a sweet fortified wine drunk before a meal to stimulate appetite.

clue.text: Element of tradition in this anniversary marked with pottery

indicators.note: Element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the custom is celebrating a wedding milestone with ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: The anniversary gift tradition assigns pottery to the ninth year of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional list of wedding anniversary gifts, pottery belongs to year nine.

clue.text: Chances putting daughters in older school initially

indicators.note: putting daughters in says the daughters piece goes within the next
in places the daughters piece within the school letters
initially picks the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them make DD

explanation.surface: Assessing the prospects of placing girls at a traditional secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are betting terms expressing the likelihood that something happens.

clue.text: Peter out with delay over and over again

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter goes out late time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' shuffles PETER and DELAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something time and again, frequently and many times, is to do it repeatedly.

clue.text: Millions without work around Democratic heartland

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: around says the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: having no work makes you idle

explanation.surface: Millions jobless across the Democrats' core states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts D inside IDLE, after M.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a land is its centre, its central region.

clue.text: Peculiar upset involving wayward act of heroism

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside
in a down clue, upset turns the word over so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: odd means peculiar
erring means straying or wayward

explanation.surface: A strange, disturbed figure is caught up in some reckless deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic daring, the bold adventurous action of old romances.

clue.text: Discard song, one planned as a hit?

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
the A-side of a single was the track the record company intended to be the hit

explanation.surface: Throw away a tune that someone meant to make a chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: On old vinyl singles the A-side carried the intended hit, the B-side the filler.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something aside and no longer use it is to discard it.

clue.text: Money, nothing less — fortune?

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: loot is slang for money
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Cash, all of it gone: what fate brings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows a fortune in the sense of fate, one's lot in life, not riches.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or fate, what fortune has allotted.

clue.text: Deviant sailor and soldier imprisoning Queen and King

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a soldier ant is a fighting caste of ant, so ant stands for soldier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
R, Rex, is the abbreviation for King

explanation.surface: A wayward pair of servicemen lock up royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier ant is a crossword staple: the fighting caste of an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant behaviour departs from the norm, which is what deviant means.

clue.text: Group of soldiers commanded to collect equipment

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Troops are ordered to gather up their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions.

clue.text: Study centre — expert securing a degree — gosh!

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the next pieces go within

parts.note: an ace is an expert
my is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: An expert lands a qualification at a college and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, a place for learning.

clue.text: Problematic situation involving power following European sovereignty

indicators.note: following places the earlier piece after the European letter
involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: being in the mire is being in trouble

explanation.surface: A crisis about power after Europe's states assert their independence.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is supreme rule over territories, imperial dominion.

clue.text: Recorded limits to the range in conclusion

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: The edges of the firing range, settled at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits to' takes the outer letters of both words, which 'in' places inside the conclusion word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something in a ledger or log is to record it.

clue.text: Amend the colour, obscuring old line?

definitions.text: Amend the colour, obscuring old line?

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so the remaining letters are reworked into a new order
obscuring means hiding, so these letters are removed from view

explanation.surface: Touching up a picture to fix its tint and hide an old crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscuring' removes O and L from THE COLOUR, leaving THECOUR, and 'Amend' rearranges it. The whole clue also describes the act, so 'Amend' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving a picture or dyed hair with small fresh touches is the craft of photographic touching-up.

clue.text: Note provided by pre-eminent modern composer

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
A-list describes the most celebrated people

explanation.surface: A note written by a leading contemporary musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pre-eminent' gives A-LIST, the top tier of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalism is a modern style of music using repeated patterns, as in Glass or Reich.

clue.text: Finally picking up note amidst a lot of notes

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads upward
amidst places a piece in the middle of another
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: music is written in notes

explanation.surface: A last-minute collection of a single banknote from a big wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims MUSIC to MUSI, 'amidst' puts N inside to make MUSNI, and 'picking up' reverses that, reading upward in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to sum up, meaning in conclusion or to put it briefly.

clue.text: Conservative compassion after leader deposed in urban area

indicators.note: a leader deposed is one ousted from the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: pity is compassion

explanation.surface: Tory sympathy runs out in the town once its chief is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is a large town, an urban settlement.

clue.text: Cold month with early closing in holiday island

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: closing early means stopping before the last letter, so the final one goes

parts.note: April is a month

explanation.surface: A chilly spring month when the shops close early on a resort island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early closing' was the half-day a British town's shops shut each week.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples popular with tourists.

clue.text: Fever limiting start of reasoned debate

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing within bounds, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of reasoned

explanation.surface: Heated feelings curbing the opening of a calm discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute or discuss a point, to put a case.

clue.text: Remove blemish in beer

indicators.note: in puts a piece inside another

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
a rip is a tear, a flaw or blemish

explanation.surface: A flaw spotted in a pint gets taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip out is to take out entirely, to extract.

clue.text: Setter's going round European capital repressed in recollection

indicators.note: going round says the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: the setter speaks of themselves, so setter's is my

indicators.note: read as re-pressed, pressed back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: The compiler roams round a capital, pushing back recollections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repressed' is read as re-pressed, pushed back, so ROME becomes EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory is something recalled from the past.

clue.text: I had number displayed in strength — 12?

indicators.note: displayed in places the pieces within the next word

parts.note: might means strength
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: Someone shows a number in bold type, here twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows 12 is one example: 12 o'clock at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night on the clock is the hour when one day turns into the next.
